title: Koszul augmentation lifts are chain homotopic
statement: For every commutative ring A, ideal I, finite tuple g in I and projective resolution P of A/I, any two chain maps from the Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] of g into P having the same composite with its augmentation in degree zero are chain homotopic. No regularity or source exactness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Part (2); adapted from Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.liftHomotopyZero and Homotopy.mkInductive

proof.text: Each Koszul term is free by exteriorPower.instFree, hence projective in ModuleCat. Subtract the two chain maps; their degree-zero difference is killed by the augmentation.

Use exactness at the augmentation to lift the degree-zero difference to degree one. Use exactness in positive degrees to lift successively the residual difference after the previous homotopy component. The chain-map equations and d²=0 show each residual is a cycle. Assemble these actual lifts with Homotopy.mkInductive and Homotopy.equivSubZero.

lean.statement:
theorem koszul_augmentation_lifts_homotopic (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    (I : Ideal A) (r : ℕ) (g : Fin r → I)
    (P : ProjectiveResolution (ModuleCat.of A (A ⧸ I)))
    (a b : ExteriorAlgebra.koszulComplex A r (fun j ↦ (g j : A)) ⟶ P.complex)
    (hab : a.f 0 ≫ P.π.f 0 = b.f 0 ≫ P.π.f 0) : Nonempty (Homotopy a b)
